description: This test validates the URL validation functionality for URLs containing port numbers in their authority component, specifically testing that the UrlValidator class correctly accepts URLs with various port configurations. Initialize the test by setting up a test parts index array where all elements except the last are reset to zero in the setUp method, which is a field of the test class of type int array. Create a new UrlValidator instance using the default constructor, which initializes the validator with default schemes and validation options. Call the isValid method on the UrlValidator instance three times with different URL strings to test port number validation: first with "http://www.apache.org:80/path" which includes the standard HTTP port 80, second with "http://www.apache.org:8/path" which uses a non-standard single-digit port 8, and third with "http://www.apache.org:/path" which contains a colon but no explicit port number. The isValid method programmatically parses the URL as a URI, validates the scheme against allowed schemes, checks the authority component including hostname and port validation through regex patterns and domain validation, and validates the path, query, and fragment components, representing the user experience of validating whether a given URL string conforms to proper URL format standards. Assert that each of the three isValid method calls returns true using assertTrue assertions, validating that URLs with explicit standard ports, non-standard ports, and empty port specifications are all considered valid by the validator. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the accuracy of decimal-to-string conversion methods by ensuring that randomly generated double values can be converted to string representations and then parsed back to their original values without loss of precision. The test exercises the ParsedDecimal class's toScientificString, toEngineeringString, and toPlainString methods with different formatting options, asserting that each conversion maintains numerical accuracy through round-trip parsing. Initialize a UniformRandomProvider using RandomSource XO_RO_SHI_RO_128_PP with a seed value of 0L for reproducible random number generation, then create two FormatOptionsImpl instances where the first uses default settings and the second is configured with setExponentSeparator set to "e" and setIncludeFractionPlaceholder set to false. Execute a loop that iterates 10,000 times, and in each iteration, call the helper method createRandomDouble with the random provider to generate a test double value by creating a 52-bit mantissa mask combined with a sign bit, applying it to a random long value, generating a random exponent between 1 and 2045, and using Double longBitsToDouble to construct the final double value. For each generated double, create a ParsedDecimal instance using the from method and convert it to string representations using toScientificString, toEngineeringString, and toPlainString with both the standard and alternative format options, then parse each resulting string back to a double using Double parseDouble and assert equality with the original double value using Assertions assertEquals, validating that the conversion process preserves the exact numerical value across all six string format combinations. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates URL encoding behavior in query parameters to ensure that the UrlValidator class correctly handles space characters in URL query strings. The test examines the application's URL validation functionality by testing three different representations of spaces in query parameters and verifying that only properly encoded spaces are accepted as valid URLs. Initialize a new UrlValidator instance using the default constructor, which configures the validator with standard validation options and default allowed schemes. Call the isValid method on the validator with the string "http://example.com/serach?address=Main Avenue" and assert that it returns false, validating that unencoded spaces in query parameters are correctly rejected as invalid URLs. Next, call the isValid method with the string "http://example.com/serach?address=Main%20Avenue" and assert that it returns true, confirming that percent-encoded spaces using %20 are properly accepted as valid URL formatting. Finally, call the isValid method with the string "http://example.com/serach?address=Main+Avenue" and assert that it returns true, verifying that plus-encoded spaces are also recognized as valid URL query parameter encoding. The isValid method programmatically parses the input string as a URI, validates the scheme against allowed protocols, checks the authority component for proper formatting, and validates the query string against established URL encoding patterns, providing comprehensive URL validation that ensures proper encoding standards are met for web applications handling user-submitted URLs. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the URL validator's behavior when configured to allow local URLs versus the default configuration that restricts them. Initialize a URL validator with the allow local URLs option enabled, then assert that it correctly validates simple hostnames like "hostname", hostnames with paths such as "hostname/test/index.html", and localhost URLs like "localhost/test/index.html" as valid. Verify that malformed hostnames containing invalid characters such as "first.my-testing" and "broke.hostname" are rejected as invalid, while standard domain names like "www.apache.org" continue to validate successfully. Create a second URL validator instance with default settings (no special options), then assert that the same hostname and localhost URLs that were previously valid are now rejected as invalid, while the standard domain URL remains valid. The test uses JUnit framework assertions to verify the expected validation outcomes for each URL string against both validator configurations.

This test validates that an IPv6 address validation capability correctly identifies a specific expanded IPv6 address format as valid. Initialize a validator component that can assess internet address formats. Execute the validation functionality against a full-form IPv6 address containing hexadecimal segments separated by colons, including both uppercase letters and numeric values. Assert that the validator returns a positive result indicating the address format is recognized as valid, confirming the validation logic properly handles this standard IPv6 notation. The testing uses JUnit framework.

Retrieve validation results for both the first name and last name fields, then assert that both field results exist and contain the expected validation action. This test validates the range checking functionality of the ByteValidator class by testing whether byte values fall within, below, or above specified minimum and maximum boundaries. The isInRange method programmatically checks if a byte value falls between inclusive minimum and maximum bounds, the minValue method verifies a value meets or exceeds a minimum threshold, and the maxValue method confirms a value does not exceed a maximum threshold, all supporting user scenarios where numeric input validation requires range constraints. This test validates the field-specific validation functionality of the validator framework by setting up a date validation scenario and verifying that a single field can be validated independently. This test validates the domain validator's top-level domain override functionality by configuring conflicting generic TLD overrides and verifying that exclusion rules take precedence over inclusion rules. First, update the domain validator's generic TLD override tables by adding a specific country code TLD like "ch" to both the generic plus override array and the generic minus override array using the TLD override update method with the appropriate array type enumerations. Next, obtain a singleton instance of the domain validator using the standard factory method. Then, validate that the TLD is not considered a valid generic TLD by calling the generic TLD validation method with the country code and asserting that it returns false, demonstrating that the minus override successfully excludes the TLD despite its presence in the plus override. Finally, verify that a standard generic TLD like "com" remains valid by calling the same validation method and asserting that it returns true, confirming that the override mechanism only affects the specifically configured TLD. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the domain validator's ability to handle static TLD override configurations and instance-specific override behaviors for both generic and country code top-level domains. The test verifies that static overrides applied through the updateTLDOverride method affect new validator instances, while instance-specific overrides can selectively restore or modify validation behavior without affecting the global static configuration. Begin by calling the DomainValidator updateTLDOverride method four times to establish static overrides: first with ArrayType.GENERIC_PLUS and the string "gp" to add a custom generic TLD, second with ArrayType.GENERIC_MINUS and "com" to remove the standard com TLD, third with ArrayType.COUNTRY_CODE_PLUS and "cp" to add a custom country code TLD, and fourth with ArrayType.COUNTRY_CODE_MINUS and "ch" to remove the standard ch country code TLD. Create a DomainValidator instance by calling getInstance with false as the parameter to disable local domain validation. Assert that the isValidGenericTld method returns true when passed "gp" to verify the custom generic TLD addition, assert that isValidGenericTld returns false when passed "com" to confirm the standard TLD removal, assert that isValidCountryCodeTld returns true for "cp" to validate the custom country code addition, and assert that isValidCountryCodeTld returns false for "ch" to confirm the country code removal. Create a new ArrayList of DomainValidator.Item objects and add two items: one Item constructed with ArrayType.GENERIC_MINUS and an empty string, and another Item with ArrayType.COUNTRY_CODE_MINUS and an empty string, which effectively clears the minus overrides for this instance. Create a new validator instance by calling getInstance with false and the items list to apply instance-specific overrides. Assert that isValidGenericTld returns true for both "gp" and "com" to verify that the instance override restored "com" validation while preserving the "gp" addition, and assert that isValidCountryCodeTld returns true for both "cp" and "ch" to confirm that the instance override restored "ch" validation while preserving the "cp" addition. Finally, create another validator instance using getInstance with false and no items list to demonstrate that the static class-level overrides remain unchanged, then assert that isValidGenericTld returns true for "gp" and false for "com", and assert that isValidCountryCodeTld returns true for "cp" and false for "ch" to confirm the static overrides persist independently of instance-specific configurations. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the format and check digit validation capabilities for American Express credit card numbers. Initialize an American Express credit card validator and extract its regular expression component to test the format requirements. Verify that the regular expression correctly rejects card numbers with lengths other than fifteen digits, accepts only numbers starting with prefixes thirty-four or thirty-seven while rejecting other prefixes, and rejects numbers containing invalid characters. Test the complete validator functionality by confirming it accepts valid American Express numbers while rejecting numbers from other credit card types like Diners, Discover, Mastercard, and Visa, and verify that validation returns the original number for valid inputs but returns null for invalid ones including those that pass format checks but fail check digit validation. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the required field validation functionality when a last name field is set to a blank string, ensuring that both first name and last name fields fail validation as expected when empty values are provided. This test validates the type conversion functionality of a validator framework when processing numeric and date values using French locale formatting conventions. Initialize a type bean object and populate its properties with string representations of various data types including a byte value of "12", a short value of "-129", an integer of "1443", a long of "88000", a float using French decimal notation "12,1555", a double with French formatting "129,1551511111", and a date in European format "21/12/2010". This test validates the American Express credit card validator component by exercising both its regular expression pattern matching and overall validation logic. Initialize a code validator instance specifically configured for American Express cards and extract its underlying regex validator component. Exercise the full validator by testing it against various predefined valid and invalid American Express numbers, asserting that the validation method returns null for invalid inputs and the original input for valid ones, and verify that the validator correctly rejects valid numbers from other card types including Diners, Discover, Mastercard, and Visa while accepting several specific valid American Express test numbers. This test validates the American Express credit card number validation functionality by testing both the regular expression pattern matching and the complete validation logic of the AMEX_VALIDATOR. Initialize a CodeValidator instance by accessing the AMEX_VALIDATOR static field from CreditCardValidator, then retrieve its RegexValidator component using the getRegexValidator method to test the underlying regular expression pattern that enforces American Express card format requirements of exactly 15 digits starting with either "34" or "37". description: This test validates that validation rule overrides function correctly when processing form field validation. Initialize a name bean and set its last name property to a valid string value. Load validation resources from an XML configuration file during setup. Construct a validator using the loaded resources and a specific form key, then register the name bean as a parameter for validation processing. Execute the validation process to obtain validation results. Assert that the results object is not null, then retrieve validation results for both first name and last name fields. Verify that the first name validation result exists and contains the expected message key for the validation action, while confirming that the last name validation result is null, demonstrating that the override rule properly excludes certain field validations. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that the Apache Commons Validator framework correctly performs locale-specific type conversion and validation for French locale formatting, specifically testing that numeric values with French decimal separators are properly converted to their corresponding Java primitive wrapper types. Initialize a new TypeBean instance and populate it with string representations of various data types using French locale formatting conventions, setting the byte field to "12", short field to "-129", integer field to "1443", long field to "88000", float field to "12,1555" with comma as decimal separator, double field to "129,1551511111" with comma as decimal separator, and date field to "21/12/2010" in day/month/year format. Call the helper method localeTest with the configured TypeBean and Locale.FRENCH as parameters, which constructs a new Validator instance using the loaded resources and "typeLocaleForm" configuration, sets the TypeBean as the BEAN_PARAM parameter and the French locale as the "java.util.Locale" parameter, then invokes the validate method to obtain ValidatorResults. Within the helper method, assert that the results are not null, retrieve the result value map, and verify that each converted value is an instance of the correct wrapper class (Byte, Short, Integer, Long, Float, Double, Date) for the French locale, then assert that no values in the result map are null. After the helper method returns the result map, assert that the float value converted from "12,1555" equals 12 when cast to Float and converted to integer with the message "float value not correct", and assert that the double value converted from "129,1551511111" equals 129 when cast to Double and converted to integer with the message "double value not correct". The testing framework used is JUnit, identified by the @Test annotation and assertion methods like assertEquals, assertNotNull, and assertInstanceOf.

This test validates the null value handling behavior of the RegexValidator class when provided with null input across its three primary validation methods. Initialize a new RegexValidator instance using the constructor with a REGEX field from the test class, which serves as the regular expression pattern for validation. Call the isValid method on the validator instance passing null as the argument, then assert that the result is false using assertFalse with the message "Instance isValid()" to verify that null input is correctly identified as invalid. Next, call the validate method on the same validator instance with null as the parameter, then assert that the returned value is null using assertNull with the message "Instance validate()" to confirm that null input produces no aggregated string result from matched groups. Finally, call the match method on the validator instance passing null as the argument, then assert that the returned value is null using assertNull with the message "Instance match()" to verify that null input produces no array of matched groups. The RegexValidator's isValid method programmatically returns false for null values without attempting pattern matching, the validate method returns null for null input without processing regex groups, and the match method returns null for null input without extracting capture groups, ensuring consistent null-safe behavior across all validation operations for users attempting to validate potentially null string values. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the behavior of a validator when the first dependent validation rule fails, ensuring that subsequent dependent validations are not executed. Initialize a name bean object to serve as the validation target, then construct a validator instance using pre-loaded validation resources and a form key. Set the name bean as a parameter on the validator using the bean parameter constant, then invoke the validate method to execute the validation rules and obtain the validation results. Assert that the results object is not null, then retrieve the validator result specifically for the middle name field and verify it is not null. Confirm that the middle name result contains the required action and that this required validation failed by checking its validity status returns false. Finally, assert that the middle name result does not contain the integer or positive validation actions, demonstrating that these dependent validations were skipped when the initial required validation failed. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

description: This test validates that a validation framework correctly processes all validation rules for a data structure containing personal name information. Initialize the test environment by loading validation configuration resources and setting up test data with predefined values for first name, middle name, and last name fields. Create a name data structure and populate it with the initialized test values, then execute the validation process using the configured validation rules and framework. Verify that all required field validations pass by checking that the first name meets its required criteria, the middle name satisfies required, integer, and positive number validations, and the last name passes both required and integer validation rules. Assert that each validation rule executes successfully and returns the expected valid results for all tested fields. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the date validation functionality of the Apache Commons Validator framework by testing both valid and invalid date formats. Initialize a validator resources object by calling a helper method that sets up date validation configuration with a property name of "date" and an action name of "date", which creates a validator action pointing to a date formatting method, establishes a form with a field that depends on the date validation action, and processes the resources. Create a test bean instance and set its date property to a valid date string like "2/3/1999", then instantiate a validator with the configured resources and form name "testForm", and set the bean as a parameter using the bean parameter constant. Execute the validation by calling the validate method and assert that the results are not null, retrieve the validator result for the date property and verify it is not null, confirm that the result contains the date action, and assert that the validation passed for the date action, catching any exceptions and failing the test if validation throws an error. Modify the test bean's date property to an invalid date string like "2/30/1999" and repeat the validation process, asserting that the results and validator result are not null, the result contains the date action, but this time verify that the validation failed for the date action, again catching exceptions and failing if validation throws an error. The testing is performed using JUnit framework.

description: This test validates the string tokenization functionality when processing text with semicolon delimiters, double quote characters, and whitespace handling. Initialize a string tokenizer with a complex input containing multiple tokens separated by semicolons, including quoted content with embedded semicolons and escaped quotes, along with empty tokens and whitespace. Configure the tokenizer to use semicolon as the delimiter character, double quote as the quote character, and set up a trimming matcher to handle whitespace while disabling the ignore empty tokens feature. Extract the complete token array from the tokenizer and verify that forward iteration through all tokens using the next method produces the expected count, then perform backward iteration through all tokens using the previous method to confirm bidirectional navigation works correctly. Assert that the resulting token array matches the expected output containing properly parsed tokens with preserved quoted content, trimmed whitespace, and null values for empty tokens, and verify that both forward and backward iteration counts equal the expected array length to ensure complete traversal capability. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the custom configuration capabilities of the engineering number format by ensuring that a formatter with specific customizations produces expected string representations for various double values. Initialize a DoubleFunction formatter by calling the builder method on the ENGINEERING constant of the DoubleFormat class, then configure it with a maximum precision of 3, minimum decimal exponent of -3, signed zero disabled, fraction placeholder disabled, comma as decimal separator, lowercase "e" as exponent separator, "inf" for infinity representation, "nan" for NaN representation, and exclamation mark as the minus sign, then call get to obtain the formatter. Execute a series of assertions using a helper method that applies the formatter to specific double values and compares the results to expected strings, validating special cases including NaN producing "nan", positive infinity producing "inf", negative infinity producing "!inf", very small values like 0.00001 and -0.0001 producing "0", and negative zero producing "0". Assert that values requiring scientific notation format correctly with the custom exponent separator and minus sign, such as 0.001 producing "1e!3", -0.01 producing "!10e!3", 1000.0 producing "1e3", and -10000.0 producing "!10e3". Verify that the custom decimal separator appears in formatted numbers like 12345 producing "12,3e3" and mathematical constants like Pi producing "3,14" and E producing "2,72". Confirm that extreme values including Double.MAX_VALUE, Double.MIN_VALUE, and Double.MIN_NORMAL format appropriately, with the latter two producing "0" due to the minimum decimal exponent configuration. The helper method applies the formatter function to each test value and uses assertEquals from the Assertions class to verify the actual output matches the expected string. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the Test annotation.

description: This test validates the copy constructor functionality for string substitution configuration. Initialize a string substitution component and configure it with specific settings including disabling value substitution, enabling variable substitution, enabling undefined variable exceptions, setting a custom escape character, configuring a value delimiter, setting a variable prefix and suffix, and assigning a null string lookup resolver. Create a new string substitution component using the copy constructor with the configured source component as the parameter. Assert that the new component correctly inherits the variable substitution enablement, undefined variable exception enablement, escape character setting, and verify that the value delimiter matcher, variable prefix matcher, and variable suffix matcher all contain the expected character configurations by checking their string representations end with the appropriate character patterns. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

Initialize a text string builder instance and test its insert method functionality with various data types and boundary conditions. Append the string "barbaz" to the builder and verify its content, then assert that inserting at invalid indices like -1 or 7 throws IndexOutOfBoundsException. Test inserting null objects and strings at valid positions to confirm they don't modify the builder content, then insert the string "foo" at index 0 and verify the result becomes "foobarbaz". Clear the builder and repeat similar tests for string insertion with null values and boundary validation. Continue testing character array insertion by verifying IndexOutOfBoundsException for invalid indices, confirming null and empty arrays don't change content, and validating successful insertion of character arrays containing "foo" at the beginning. Test character array insertion with offset and length parameters, ensuring proper exception handling for invalid array bounds, null arrays, and out-of-range offset/length combinations, while confirming successful partial array insertion. Proceed to test boolean value insertion by verifying boundary exceptions and successful insertion of true and false values at the beginning, observing how they convert to their string representations. Test character insertion with boundary validation and successful insertion of the exclamation mark character. Continue with integer, long, float, and double value insertions, each time clearing the builder, appending "barbaz", testing boundary conditions with IndexOutOfBoundsException assertions, and verifying successful insertion of sample values like 0, 1, 2.3, and 4.5 at index 0. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

Initialize a string builder instance and append the text "barbaz" to establish a baseline state, then verify the content matches "barbaz" using string conversion. Test the insert method's boundary validation by attempting to insert a constant string value at invalid negative and out-of-bounds indices, confirming that IndexOutOfBoundsException is thrown for both cases. Insert a null object at index zero and verify the content remains unchanged as "barbaz", then insert the constant string at index zero and confirm the result becomes "foobarbaz". Clear the builder and repeat the process with string insertion, testing the same boundary conditions with negative and excessive indices, inserting null and valid strings at index zero, and verifying the expected concatenated results. Continue this pattern for character array insertion, testing with null arrays, empty arrays, and valid character arrays containing the letters 'f', 'o', 'o', while validating boundary exceptions. Test character array insertion with offset and length parameters, verifying exceptions for invalid offsets, lengths, and boundary conditions, then confirm successful insertion of a substring from a larger character array. Repeat the testing approach for boolean values (true and false), single characters, integers, long values, float values, and double values, ensuring each data type correctly converts to its string representation and inserts at the specified position while maintaining proper boundary validation. The test uses the JUnit testing framework.
